claim: Any duration ('N min') counts as the rider admitting lateness. So the most common way a rider contests a no-show, saying how long they have waited, reads LATE, and the fee is upheld with tier AUTO. The comment at lines 27-29 says LATE needs a first-person delay and that a message the lists cannot settle falls to UNCLEAR, never to an automatic uphold. That is not what the code does.
action: fixed: durations are no longer admissions; 'I wait 10 min already', 'waiting for 5 mins' read PLACES

claim: Questions to the driver read LATE when they lack a question mark, which is usual in Singlish chat ('u on the way ah', 'u still coming ah'). The question patterns need '?', 'or not' or 'anot', or a leading are/r/is, and _WHO has no 'the driver'. Bare 'on the way', 'omw', 'otw', 'reaching' and 'almost there' in RIDER_LATE_PHRASES (line 55) have no second-person exclusion. Round 1 finding ENG-1 is therefore fixed only for questions written with '?'.
action: fixed: questions about the driver need no question mark ('u still coming ah', 'Is the driver on the way'); the reader now reads LATE only when the whole message is known admissions and filler

claim: A 'where' question outside the narrow list, combined with an admission, reads LATE instead of UNCLEAR. The card says asking where the driver is contests presence, and a message that fits both readings is unclear (reading test, approval). Bare 'where?', Singlish 'u where' and 'car where', 'which side/lane', 'where did u park' and 'still not arrive?' are not presence cues, and _PLACE_WORDS does not include them.
action: fixed: any 'where' and a message ending in a question are presence cues; 'coming down, where?' reads UNCLEAR

claim: Malay, Hokkien and Chinese arrival words ('sampai', 'dah sampai', 'dao le', '到了', '楼下') are not place cues. Alone they read UNCLEAR, which is safe, but with any LATE token the message reads LATE and the fee is upheld automatically. The English equivalent reads UNCLEAR.
action: fixed: Malay and Chinese arrival words (sampai, dao le, kat, mana, tunggu, the Chinese for 'arrived' and 'downstairs') are place cues; unknown words keep a message out of LATE

claim: Rider messages that quote the driver ('you said coming') or contest the timing ('you early, my booking is 8.45') read LATE. The only exclusion for driver-directed wording is the (?<!you )(?<!u ) lookbehind directly before 'coming'. 'said/say', 'early', 'you late' and 'map wrong' are not contest cues. In the DISP-002 shape the timing claim changes the outcome.
action: fixed: quoting the driver and 'you early' or 'you late' are contest cues; such messages read PLACES or UNCLEAR

claim: Common lateness admissions read PLACES and are escalated to a person: the over-escalation FX1 set out to remove. Any "I'm at <X>" places the rider unless X is home, work, office or school (line 43). '^reach' and 'i reach' (line 45) catch 'reach soon'. "I'm there" (line 42) catches "I'm there soon". 'at (the) <spot>' (line 46) and 'not at the pick' (line 52) fire inside 'almost at the lobby' and "I'm not at the pickup yet".
action: fixed: 'reach soon', 'I'm there soon', 'I'm at the lift', 'almost at the lobby', 'not at the lobby yet' no longer read PLACES (0 over-escalations in the 428-message corpus)

claim: The reader ignores order within a message. One message that admits lateness and then places the rider reads UNCLEAR (APPROVE), while the same words sent as two messages give STRONG (HUMAN). The card's credibility_note says a rider who reaches the pick-up before the cancellation does contest the no-show. Separately, many placing or contesting messages fall to UNCLEAR instead of PLACES.
action: not changed: one message that admits lateness and then places the rider is UNCLEAR (approval) by the card's 'fits both readings' rule; recorded in D27 for the team

claim: Some plain admissions read UNCLEAR, so routine late riders get an approval-tier uphold instead of AUTO.
action: reduced: fewer admissions fall to UNCLEAR; the rest cost an approval only, by design

claim: Since A1, the CW-F06 card counts a notification failure only if it is logged during the wait, but the reference engine still counts a rider_notified failure logged at any time as STRONG. A1 windowed rider GPS two lines above and left this check unwindowed.
action: fixed in the card: a notification failure counts whenever it is logged for the trip, as in v0.1 (the A1 rewrite had narrowed it by accident); the engine already did this

claim: The rider explanation says 'There is no GPS trace from your phone in the trip record' whenever rider evidence is not STRONG, even when the case has rider GPS: points away from the pin, or points outside the window A1 moved to the arrival indication (the D30 case for GPS). This is the GPS half of round 1 finding M1; the fix covered calls and messages only.
action: fixed: the rider explanation says the phone's GPS points do not show the rider at the pick-up when the case has rider GPS

claim: The card treats only admissions of lateness or still being on the way (and acknowledgments) as 'not counter-evidence', and sends a message that fits neither reading to the reading test. The engine's LATE list also catches the rider's own wrong-place admissions without a place word. Such messages are upheld AUTO, near-identical wording goes to APPROVE, and the rider is told the message 'said you were running late or still on your way'.
action: fixed: wrong-place admissions ('my bad', 'I went to the wrong building') read UNCLEAR, not LATE

claim: D27 and D28 are marked decide: done, but the record shows only that Jasper confirmed four case outcomes, not the rule designs. D28 also says FC-R00 has 'credibility D, like CW-R00', but CW-R00 is credibility B.
action: fixed: D27 and D28 name the open team and organizer confirmations (new question O14); D28 no longer calls CW-R00 a D rule

claim: In V66 the rider is told that their 'yes' 'does not clearly say whether you were at the pick-up point', though it answers the driver's 'Are you at the lobby now?', and the driver had said 'I've arrived at the pickup point, I'm at the lobby area'. The card's 'a bare "yes"' example and the engine read a reply without the message it answers.
action: not changed: a bare 'yes' is unclear on purpose (the card's example); the reading test sends it to approval

claim: PB-CW-WAITING reads CW-F06 (step 8) after the advocates' briefs (step 7, GEN-R05). PB-CW-NOSHOW reads it (step 11) before the briefs (step 13, 'citing findings and evidence IDs only'). In the waiting playbook the briefs are therefore written before F-RIDER-EVIDENCE exists.
action: fixed: PB-CW-WAITING reads CW-F06 (step 7) before the advocates' briefs (step 8)

claim: Some descriptions of CW-F06 are still in pre-A1 terms (the round 1 m1 fix covered only the taxonomy label and one ontology note). The scope competency question asks 'Is there rider-side system evidence?' answered by CW-F06. The annotation_schema rider_contacts column defines CW-F06's input as 'between the arrival and the cancellation', which is wrong for waiting fees. The ontology still ties NO_RIDER_EVIDENCE to the missing rider GPS trace.
